candidate.educational_objective: Explain the function and limitation of smart-pump dose error-reduction software.

options.A: It compares the programmed dose or rate with preconfigured limits in the drug library and alerts the nurse when a setting falls outside those limits.
options.B: It independently chooses the correct medication without any nurse input.
options.C: It automatically corrects every programming error without alerting the nurse.
options.D: It removes the need for the nurse to verify the medication, dose, route, or pump settings.

candidate.rationale: FDA defines a smart pump as an infusion pump with medication-error prevention software that can alert the operator when a programmed setting is outside preconfigured limits. The nurse must still respond to alerts and perform the clinical and medication verification required for safe administration.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Smart-pump medication-error prevention software alerts operators when programmed settings fall outside preconfigured limits.
candidate.source_document_title: Infusion Pump Glossary; Infusion Pump Risk Reduction Strategies for Clinicians
candidate.source_locator: Smart pump definition—alerts for settings outside preconfigured limits; clinician risk-reduction guidance—use drug library and respond to alerts
candidate.stem: A nurse programs an infusion using a smart pump with dose error-reduction software. How does this feature help reduce medication errors?
